extracted.intended_audience: recipients of Federal financial assistance, Title IX Coordinators, and school administrators responsible for Title IX compliance
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts regulatory standards and expectations for Title IX Coordinators and recipients under final §106.44(f), including when coordinators must act, what actions are required, limits on scope, delegation/authority, and obligations to remedy and prevent sex discrimination across education programs and activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title IX Coordinator responsibility for coordinating recipient compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient's Title IX Coordinator is responsible for coordinating a recipient's compliance with its obligations under Title IX and this part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department revised §106.44(f) to make clear the Title IX Coordinator's role stems from the recipient's obligations and that the recipient remains ultimately responsible for ensuring compliance; the Coordinator's role is one of coordination and oversight, not a transfer of recipient liability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinator oversight of patterns, trends, and risk factors
rubrics_metrics.description: Title IX Coordinators must respond to patterns, trends, and risk factors and coordinate responses to individual reports and actions to prevent future sex discrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This oversight role includes monitoring institutional patterns and coordinating action to address and prevent sex discrimination for all participants in the recipient's education program or activity to help provide an environment free from sex discrimination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Early intervention, equitable treatment, and supportive measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Title IX Coordinators must coordinate early intervention efforts in response to possible sex discrimination; ensure consistent, equitable treatment of complainants and respondents; and provide supportive measures and resources to end sex discrimination and prevent its recurrence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These duties are reflected in §106.44(f)(1)(i)-(iii) and mirror obligations from §106.44(a) (2020 amendments) but are incorporated into a broader coordinated response under the final rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application to conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination (not limited to sexual harassment)
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.44(f) applies to information about any conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination under Title IX or this part, not only sexual harassment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department intended these requirements to cover a broader range of sex discrimination than the 2020 amendments; however, application is limited to conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination (see below on 'reasonably may constitute').

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient remains ultimately responsible for Title IX compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Designating a Title IX Coordinator does not shift statutory or regulatory responsibility from the recipient to the Coordinator; the recipient is responsible for compliance with Title IX obligations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The preamble emphasizes that the Department will hold the recipient responsible for meeting obligations under the regulations even as the Coordinator is required to coordinate compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure Coordinator has appropriate authority, support, and resources
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient must ensure the Title IX Coordinator is effective by giving appropriate authority, support, and resources; the Coordinator must not be a designation 'in name only.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department expects recipients to structure and support the Title IX Coordinator role so the Coordinator can effectively coordinate compliance; resources and authority should be commensurate with duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted delegation and multiple Title IX Coordinators/designees
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients may designate more than one employee to serve as a Title IX Coordinator and may delegate specific duties to designees; Title IX Coordinators may delegate responsibilities (e.g., offering and coordinating supportive measures).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delegation enables recipients to assign duties to personnel best positioned to perform them, avoid conflicts of interest, and align responsibilities with institutional administrative structure (see discussion of §106.44(g) and §106.8(a)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordination across institutional offices and leveraging existing structures
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients may coordinate Title IX compliance among offices such as dean of students, academic affairs, student conduct, HR, counseling services, and disability support as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR's enforcement experience shows a range of administrative oversight structures; recipients should use coordination similar to other institutional oversight functions to ensure effective compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training on bias, impartiality, and conflict identification
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must train Title IX Coordinators on bias and impartiality so Coordinators can identify situations in which they may be biased or conflicted out of taking particular actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See §106.8(d)(2)(iii) and (4); if a conflict or bias calls into question the efficacy of a Coordinator's actions, the recipient should ensure an alternative individual resolves the concern to avoid conflict of interest or biased determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title IX Coordinator may initiate complaints in limited, discretionary circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: Title IX Coordinators are permitted to initiate a formal complaint (i.e., sign/file a complaint) under limited circumstances as set out in §106.44(f)(1)(v) and related paragraphs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department notes this authority is longstanding but final regulations include guardrails (paragraphs (v) and (vi)) to protect complainant autonomy and safety; Coordinators should balance complainant wishes against the recipient's duty to address and prevent sex discrimination and will apply discretion rather than initiate complaints in all cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prompt and effective action requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient must take prompt and effective action to prevent, eliminate, and remedy sex discrimination in its education program or activity when notified of conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is no fixed timeframe for 'prompt'; promptness is judged in context of providing programs free from sex discrimination. 'Effective' means taking reasonable, calibrated steps based on available information and reevaluating and taking additional steps if initial measures fail to end discrimination (see discussion of §106.44(f)(1) and related enforcement expectations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to remedy the effects of sex discrimination
rubrics_metrics.description: When a recipient determines that sex discrimination occurred, it must provide and implement remedies to restore or preserve equal access to the education program or activity for the complainant or others affected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This duty follows the definition of 'remedies' in §106.2 and the Title IX statute. If a recipient's own response discriminated based on sex (e.g., via policy or implementation), the recipient must provide remedies and take additional action to prevent recurrence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trigger for Coordinator obligations: 'reasonably may constitute sex discrimination'
rubrics_metrics.description: The Title IX Coordinator requirements in §106.44(f)(1) are triggered when the Coordinator is notified of conduct that 'reasonably may constitute sex discrimination' under Title IX or this part, unless the Coordinator reasonably determines the conduct as alleged could not constitute sex discrimination under §106.44(f)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department clarified this to avoid obligating Coordinators to address conduct that on its face could not constitute sex discrimination; Coordinators may use judgment and institutional perspective (including knowledge of prior incidents) to assess whether the notification warrants action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinator may exempt notifications that could not reasonably constitute sex discrimination
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.44(f)(2) allows a Title IX Coordinator to determine that the conduct as alleged could not constitute sex discrimination, in which case the §106.44(f)(1) requirements do not apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provision addresses concerns about burden and prevents requiring Coordinators to satisfy administrative obligations for allegations that, on their face, cannot meet Title IX standards; recipients still have obligations under §106.44(a) for conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific actions required under §106.44(f)(1) (i)-(vii)
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.44(f)(1) enumerates specific actions a Title IX Coordinator must take when notified of conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination, including (i)-(iii) treating complainants and respondents equitably, offering supportive measures, and providing information about grievance procedures; (v) discretion to initiate a complaint; and (vii) taking steps to ensure sex discrimination does not continue or recur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paragraph (f)(1) operationalizes 'prompt and effective' action. Paragraph (vii) also references 'other appropriate prompt and effective steps' that may be outside a recipient's formal grievance procedures. The Department emphasizes these actions together advance the Coordinator's responsibility to respond to and prevent sex discrimination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance complainant autonomy with institutional duty when considering initiation
rubrics_metrics.description: When determining whether to initiate a complaint, Title IX Coordinators should balance complainant autonomy and safety against the recipient's obligation to address and prevent sex discrimination in its education program or activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The preamble discusses commenters' concerns (e.g., potential chilling effects, due process for respondents, parents' rights, third-party complaints, egregious conduct declined for safety reasons) and notes the Department has included guardrails and expects Coordinators to consider relevant factors rather than mechanically initiating complaints in all cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-confidential employees' reporting duties to Coordinator
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must train and require their non-confidential employees to report information about conduct they believe reasonably may constitute sex discrimination to the Title IX Coordinator under §106.44(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This reporting obligation ensures Coordinators are made aware of possible sex discrimination, but the Coordinator may nonetheless determine that some reports do not reasonably constitute sex discrimination and therefore need not trigger §106.44(f)(1) actions.
